title: Prescriptions Desk System Card: Replacing Lost or Stolen Medication
content:
When a patient's medication from a Kestrel Prescriptions record was lost or stolen, a refill with the fill reason lost or stolen replacement may be dispensed before the refill-eligible date. The days it carries are the theft replacement days supply.

## Governing rule

- Every condition of the Prescriptions early refill rules, refill authorization rules and refill-eligible date rules continues to apply, except the police-report sentence replaced here. The replacement consumes one refill.
- A lost-or-stolen replacement refill is dispensed only when the patient states the police report number, which is recorded verbatim on the replacement, wherever the class requires a police report number and also, in any class, wherever the replacement carries 30 or more days of supply. The number is what the patient states; it is copied exactly as given.
- The replacement never brings back owed units that were cancelled: a cancelled balance stays undispensed.

## Conditions of the replacement

A lost-or-stolen replacement refill is not dispensed until the fill it replaces carries no open owed balance, its owed units having been completed or cancelled on the ledger.

The theft replacement days supply is fixed only after every confirmed mislabeled-directions report on the prescription is matched by a corrected remake on the ledger.

In the words of the records: an owed-balance entry still open on the replaced fill holds the replacement back, and a confirmed wrong-directions-label report with no corrected remake on the ledger leaves the days supply unfixed.

## Capability of the tool

`record_theft_replacement_refill_fbe8d6a8` dispenses a replacement for medication the patient lost or had stolen, ahead of the prescription's refill-eligible date, and books it on the fill ledger as a lost-or-stolen replacement refill. One call books one refill entry with the fill reason `lost_or_stolen_replacement`, dispensed complete today at the store holding the prescription and ready for pickup today. It records the police report number the patient gave, consumes one authorized refill, records the refill sequence number and the refills left, and lowers the prescription's remaining refills by one. After the call the replacement is waiting in will-call and the prescription shows one refill fewer.

## How it is invoked

The tool belongs to the agent. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`, naming `record_theft_replacement_refill_fbe8d6a8`.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `prescription_id` | the reference number of the prescription record being replaced, as returned by the prescription lookup for the verified patient | text identifier |
| `days_supply_dispensed` | the days of therapy the replacement carries | an integer count of days, no decimals |
| `police_report_number` | the police report number exactly as the patient states it in the conversation | verbatim: copied character for character with the same digits, letters and punctuation, nothing added, removed or reformatted |

## Return

A text rendering of a dictionary: `fill_id` (text, the new fill-ledger reference), `prescription_id` (text), `fill_number` (integer refill sequence number), `fill_reason` (text, always "lost_or_stolen_replacement"), `days_supply_dispensed` (integer days), `police_report_number` (text, as recorded), `refills_remaining_after` (integer refills left), `ready_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, today) and `status` (text, "replacement_booked" when the entry was written).
